question:
A closed cylindrical container is required to have a volume of $432\pi\ \text{cm}^3$.

(a) Express its total surface area as a function of its radius $r$.

(b) Using the second derivative test, determine the radius and height for which the total surface area is minimum.

(c) Calculate the minimum total surface area.
explanation:
(a)
The volume of the cylinder is
$$\pi r^2h=432\pi$$
Therefore,
$$h=\frac{432}{r^2}$$
The total surface area of a closed cylinder is
$$S=2\pi r^2+2\pi rh$$
Substituting the value of $h$,
$$S(r)=2\pi r^2+2\pi r\left(\frac{432}{r^2}\right)$$
$$S(r)=2\pi r^2+\frac{864\pi}{r}$$

(b)
Differentiating,
$$S'(r)=4\pi r-\frac{864\pi}{r^2}$$
For a stationary value,
$$4\pi r-\frac{864\pi}{r^2}=0$$
$$4r^3=864$$
$$r^3=216$$
$$r=6\ \text{cm}$$
The corresponding height is
$$h=\frac{432}{(6)^2}=12\ \text{cm}$$
Also,
$$S''(r)=4\pi+\frac{1728\pi}{r^3}$$
At $r=6$,
$$S''(6)=4\pi+\frac{1728\pi}{216}=12\pi>0$$
Hence, the total surface area is minimum for $r=6\ \text{cm}$ and $h=12\ \text{cm}$.

(c)
The minimum surface area is
$$S(6)=2\pi(6)^2+2\pi(6)(12)$$
$$S(6)=72\pi+144\pi=216\pi\ \text{cm}^2$$

options.A:
(a) $S(r)=2\pi r^2+\frac{432\pi}{r}$
(b) $r=6$ cm, $h=12$ cm
(c) Minimum area $180\pi$ cm$^2$
options.B:
(a) $S(r)=\pi r^2+\frac{864\pi}{r}$
(b) $r=12$ cm, $h=3$ cm
(c) Minimum area $288\pi$ cm$^2$
options.C:
(a) $S(r)=2\pi r^2+\frac{864\pi}{r}$
(b) $r=6$ cm, $h=12$ cm
(c) Minimum area $216\pi$ cm$^2$
options.D:
(a) $S(r)=2\pi r^2+864\pi r$
(b) $r=3$ cm, $h=48$ cm
(c) Minimum area $306\pi$ cm$^2$
